own-agent-evidence.why: R2b: the sshd escape rests on these bytes: the real sshd, its private config lines, and no board, event, window or keychain route.

no-nsapplication.why: R2b, C2b-F1: 0 of 13 pasteboard programs hold NSApplication, the route that lets AppKit reach the general board on its own.

no-event-post.why: R2b: the window route is safe because of the payload's bytes: no CGEventPost, no flag state read.

no-owner-tty.why: R2b: the PTY line opens only what a test made itself: no path to a terminal by name, no TIOCSTI.

key-route.why: R2b: the SecurityServer line stands for one route, a test key by SecKeyCreateRandomKey. The screen forbids the other Security families.

needs:larsal-window.why: The app code, HiddenLaunch and ScreenProtection among it, how it starts hidden, and the app09 program that starts it. What decides whether key events are posted is pinned too: autotype.rs holds the post flag and autotype_typing.rs sets it and picks the real keyboard or the recorder; instance.rs and lib.rs answer hidden; typing.rs asks before each key; keyboard.rs calls CGEventPost; Cargo.toml holds the build profiles and .cargo/config.toml chooses where crates come from; a line added to either could turn debug assertions off, and hidden() is always false without them. The whole autotype crate is pinned, so a new key event caller there takes the line too. macos/Larsal holds the Swift call.

workspace:larsal-sshagent/own_agent.why: This row holds the sshd no-sandbox line. The test starts /usr/sbin/sshd itself with its private config, own_agent.rs line 1889; the crate tree is what it links. The blob pin names the file so a reader sees it; the tree pin moves with any file in the crate. Every workspace crate it links is pinned too: the five named in the manifests' normal dependencies, walked from larsal-sshagent, and crates/log, which the workspace lane links through larsal-platform's net feature, ureq and ureq-proto. Read from the Cargo.toml files and the proof run's build fingerprints. larsal-server and larsal-proto are in the lock's closure only through larsal-platform's dev-dependencies, so they are not linked. The root Cargo.toml, .cargo/config.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml and vendor/ choose what those crates are and what third-party code they link: a dependency renamed with package =, a [patch] or a vendored crate's change takes this row to base too. The workspace lane also builds larsal-files, larsal-folders, larsal-hwkey, larsal-proto, larsal-qr, larsal-server, larsal-share and uniffi-bindgen, which no other row pins, and a build script in one can rewrite this program's bytes, so they are pinned here too.
